buyer.rubric: The buyer is whoever owns the decision to engage an outside recruiter for technical hiring, or who owns the headcount those hires fill inside an MSP or IT-delivery organization. Positives are the owner, founder, CEO, president, or managing partner at a smaller MSP where that person personally decides on hiring spend; the COO, chief services officer, chief customer officer, or VP/director of service delivery, operations, managed services, or professional services who owns the technical headcount at larger MSPs; the head of people, HR director, VP of people, director of talent acquisition, or recruiting manager who owns the recruiting relationship itself; and a market or regional president at a roll-up who owns a regional P&L and its hiring. Influencers who feel the pain but rarely sign a recruiter include service desk managers, NOC managers, engineering managers, team leads, and the CTO/CIO at an MSP unless that person is also a founder running a small shop. Hard negatives who carry senior titles but are not buyers for this purchase include the CFO, controller, or finance director who approve but don't choose recruiters; VP/director of sales, account executives, account managers, and marketing leaders who sit on the revenue side; a CISO or vCISO delivering security as a client service rather than owning internal hiring; individual engineers, technicians, analysts, project managers, and consultants; board members, investors, and advisors; and anyone at a parent private-equity firm rather than at the MSP itself. The exception is company size: at MSPs under roughly 150 people, the owner or founder personally makes this call even though at larger organizations that decision moves down to a VP/director of service delivery or a dedicated recruiting/HR owner.

seller.competitorTest: A competitor in this space sells generalized IT staffing or contract-technical placement to any company needing short-term technical bodies, whether or not the buyer runs a client-facing managed-services practice.

description:
Aris Search's buyers are managed service providers, and secondarily IT solutions firms and IT-department-heavy companies in verticals like SaaS, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, accounting, entertainment, engineering, logistics, and industrial, who need to fill technical and service-delivery seats (help desk, field tech, project engineer, vCIO, NOC, cloud, security, service-delivery leadership) or the sales/PM roles that support that delivery engine. The test for any candidate organisation is not whether it touches managed IT at all, but who inside it owns the relationship with the end customer receiving the technical service — that is the buyer of talent, not whoever merely consumes IT internally.

Qualifying shape is a company with a real managed-services or IT-delivery book of business, anywhere in the USA, ranging from owner-run shops under roughly 150 employees up through regional and multi-location MSP roll-ups with dedicated operations and HR functions. There is a dead zone at the very bottom and very top of the market: solo or sub-10-person shops that hire so rarely they never engage an outside recruiter sit cold on one end, and large enterprises with fully internal IT departments and their own talent-acquisition teams (rather than an MSP delivering to external clients) sit cold on the other end.

The fit verticals are IT Managed Services Providers first, IT Solutions Firms second, and then any SaaS, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, accounting, entertainment, engineering, logistics, or industrial company that runs enough internal IT infrastructure to need the same technical hiring support. Excluded is the customer base of the generalist staffing category: companies that need any short-term contract technical body regardless of whether the requester runs a client-facing managed-services practice, since that buyer cares about headcount speed rather than MSP culture fit, technical depth, or client-facing soft skills.

A recent job posting (within the last 30 days) for help desk, NOC, field tech, project engineer, or service-delivery leadership signals live hiring pain. An announcement of a private-equity-backed MSP roll-up or acquisition (within the last 12 months) signals a buyer building regional headcount fast. A newly hired COO, VP of Service Delivery, or VP of Managed Services (within the last 6 months) signals a fresh decision-maker for technical hiring. A newly created or filled Head of People, HR Director, or Recruiting Manager role at an MSP (within the last 6 months) signals an active recruiting-relationship owner. A press release or case study citing headcount growth targets or a client-count expansion (within the last 12 months) signals near-term hiring need. A testimonial or review mentioning high technician turnover or difficulty filling technical roles (within the last 12 months) signals active pain. Sponsorship of or attendance at an MSP or channel-partner event (within the last 12 months) signals an active, growing MSP. Inclusion on an MSP 500/501-style ranking list (within the last 12 months) signals scale sufficient to need outside recruiting help.

requirements.text: Operates a managed-services or IT-delivery practice (MSP, IT solutions firm, or a company in SaaS, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, accounting, entertainment, engineering, logistics, or industrial running enough internal IT infrastructure) that owns the relationship with the end customer receiving the technical service, rather than merely consuming IT internally.
Has more than roughly 10 employees and is not a large enterprise with a fully internal IT department and its own talent-acquisition team.
Is based and operating anywhere in the USA.
Is not the kind of buyer served by generalist staffing firms, i.e. one seeking any short-term contract technical body regardless of client-facing MSP culture fit, technical depth, or soft skills.
Has posted a job within the last 30 days for a help desk, NOC, field tech, project engineer, or service-delivery leadership role.
Has announced a private-equity-backed MSP roll-up or acquisition within the last 12 months.
Has hired a new COO, VP of Service Delivery, or VP of Managed Services within the last 6 months.
Has created or filled a Head of People, HR Director, or Recruiting Manager role at an MSP within the last 6 months.
Has published a press release or case study citing headcount growth targets or client-count expansion within the last 12 months.
Has a testimonial or review mentioning high technician turnover or difficulty filling technical roles within the last 12 months.
Has sponsored or attended an MSP or channel-partner event within the last 12 months.
Appears on an MSP 500/501-style ranking list within the last 12 months.
